verdicts.title: Ergonomic surprises: fix N * Cls reflected array sugar and honor pop's explicit default=None
verdicts.issues: Verified: __rmul__ metaclass dispatch fixed (4*UInt8 == UInt8*4 -> Array, reproduced); pop sentinel honored in all three backends (pop(99,None)->None, pop(99,9)->9, pop(99)->IndexError, reproduced); BoundBits.pop conditional forwarding works; full suite 854/854 with zero test edits for this pattern (re-run independently on a fresh pristine copy); composition with bitvector-behavior-8 verified (its rewritten prologue retains 'if default is not None', so the one-line sentinel swap slots in). Differential fuzz sometimes passes default=None -- lockstep preserved since all three backends change identically. NITS: (1) the designer's internal apply script misses the pop signature line (the def carries a trailing '# type: ignore' comment its pattern doesn't match) -- replaying it verbatim leaves default=None with a _MISSING guard, making BitVector().pop() return None (3 test failures); their own scratch copy was hand-corrected and the JSON checklist prescribes the right signature, so the proposal is sound, but a mechanical re-application must not trust that script. (2) pop line numbers cited (native:1143-1163 / 1144) are from their patched copy; pristine has the signature at native:1134-1135 and the guard at 1158. (3) behavior-8's after-text also rewrites the BoundBits.pop comment this solution's edit anchors on -- trivial merge, not called out.

verdicts.title: Name the field: thread the field name into every structs.py store-path error
verdicts.issues: Verified: all slots for ALL field kinds are '_bm_'+name (structs.py:737), so the [4:] idiom holds for Array/Buffer/Float too; befores verbatim (patch applied cleanly against pristine); all five claimed after-outputs reproduced exactly on the patched copy; no test pins OverflowError anywhere; NarrowingList item writes and Array.__call__ still call _coerce_one/_coerce_seq without ctx and keep working; suite 854/854 with zero test edits. NITS: (1) the behavior sentence 'wrong-type float store ValueError -> TypeError' only holds for non-str inputs (float(None)->TypeError branch); a non-numeric STRING still raises ValueError -- s.f='nope' -> "field 'f': 'nope' does not fit a Float32 (could not convert string to float: 'nope')" -- exception type unchanged and the 'does not fit' phrasing is slightly off for a type mistake (matches CPython's float() ValueError convention, but the claim overstates the normalization). (2) Adjacent unpatched bare-error paths remain: float ARRAY elements (structs.py:1426 element(float(value)).value) still leak bare OverflowError, and _BytesField's bytes(value) can raise a bare TypeError before the length check -- both outside the four covered findings, worth folding in.

verdicts.title: Honest error text: name BitVector (not the backend), both lengths, the operation, and real type names
verdicts.issues: Verified: all cited raise/docstring sites verbatim at the claimed lines (ctor native:254/speedup:341/bwbs:244; equal-length speedup:874-875/native:745-746; bwbs index/rindex 1392/1425; from_int blocks in all three backends; 5 YType messages + 3 stale docstrings; 12 fixed.py raise sites; utils 40/45/51). Three-backend claims spot-checked: bwbs r/i bitwise variants all funnel through __and__/__or__/__xor__; pristine bwbs & mismatch raises the C-level 'bitarrays of equal length expected'; pristine bwbs index(True) raises C-level 'True not in bitarray' bypassing line 1392 -- all as claimed. Ctor ValueError->TypeError: grepped the whole suite; test_construction_invalid_source_type (x3) is genuinely the only pin, and 854/854 reproduces after the quoted 2-line edit. Oracle claim verified: aggregate_types.py imports these functions FROM _legacy_aggregate (single copy, no second path); YType exists only there; parity/fastpath tests green on the patched copy. All claimed after-outputs reproduced. ISSUES (nits): (1) the proposed parity regression test ('three backends emit IDENTICAL text for index() miss, int and subsequence needles') would FAIL as the fix is specified: for a subsequence needle bwbs's new except-wrap interpolates the already-coerced value -> "BitVector('11') is not in BitVector" vs native/speedup "11 is not in BitVector"; the wrap should capture the pre-coercion value (or use .to01()). (2) The remove() wrap is in the checklist but absent from the verified scratch copy -- bwbs.remove(1) still leaks '1 not in bitarray' there, so 'ALL runtime patterns applied' overclaims by one line; the proposed wrap itself is correct. (3) 'native:745-746 identical' -- the raise is identical but the guard line differs (len(other._bits) vs other._len). (4) classproperty 'setter/deleter branches unreachable in-tree (read-only uses only)' -- string.py:212 defines a classproperty WITH a setter (codepoint_changes), so 'read-only uses only' is wrong, though the fset-is-None ERROR branches indeed have no in-tree trigger.

verdicts.title: Validate at the source: mint/entry-point checks instead of deep, late failures
verdicts.issues: Verified: befores verbatim (clean apply); all pristine 'observed today' lines reproduced (mint-then-LookupError, min_bit_length None, NoneType '<=' TypeError, raw struct.error, bare 'No conversion found'); all after-outputs reproduced on the patched copy including the wrap-retry regression pack_tuple([5,300]) -> b'\x05,' and the registered-type hint ['bool','float','int','str'] on all three raise paths (get_conversion_info, pytype_to_bits, bits_to_pytype checked). Sibling error-shape claim confirmed (int.py:137-138, 301-302). plans-2 composition claim accurate (arity pre-check at top of pack_tuple). pytypes dead-loop deletion is behavior-neutral (was never registered; suite green) and the delete-vs-uncomment decision is honestly flagged. Suite 854/854 with zero test edits for this pattern. NIT: 'the exact shape its siblings already use' is embellished -- siblings use plain {bin_format} with no !r and no choices list; the new message adds both (an improvement, not the exact shape).

verdicts.title: Lookup failures should teach: list the valid choices and point at the real knob
verdicts.issues: Verified: plans.py:318 KeyError and fields.py:88-91 verbatim; after-outputs reproduced (ValueError listing fields; f8 AttributeError teaching message; u31 still mints; q8 gets the plain message); no test pins KeyError anywhere (structs_test:1155 expects ValueError from byte_offset on a sub-byte field -- the line-328 sibling, unaffected); f16/f32/f64 confirmed as real module attributes (fields.py:79-81) so __getattr__ never fires for them; suite 854/854 with zero test edits. Both moots genuine and accepted (docs-misc-3 renames Config->SignedConfig at int.py:545/561; narrowing-5 re-exports NarrowingConfig/NarrowingWarning + __all__). ISSUE (nit): the claim "'from bytemaker.fields import f8' wraps the message in ImportError but preserves the text" is FALSE -- verified: the from-import form raises Python's own "cannot import name 'f8' from 'bytemaker.fields'" with no cause/context chaining, so the teaching text is lost for from-imports and only surfaces on attribute/getattr access (the after block only shows the getattr form, which is correct). The original finding's verifyReason stated this correctly; the solution mis-restated it.

verdicts.title: Discoverability: package re-exports, undocumented params, the stub's 64-bit cliff, and runtime deprecation signals
verdicts.issues: Verified: conversions/__init__ proposal names real modules/functions (aggregate_types entry points, conversions.ctypes_, pytypes helpers all exist); structs.py:655-657 and bittype.py:350-352 before-quotes verbatim; fields.pyi:162 '-> Any' quote exact; u128/s128/u256/s256 map to real bittypes exports (UInt128/SInt128/UInt256/SInt256 import OK); 'import warnings' is at bittype.py:6. Deprecation item verified end-to-end on an independent patched copy: _legacy_aggregate.py:121/176 are exactly 'return unit.to_bits()' / 'return unittype.from_bits(unitbits)' and the redirects are behavior-identical to the deprecated method bodies (return self.bits / cls(bits=bits)); after warnings+redirect the plain suite gives 54 warnings exactly as claimed and -W error::DeprecationWarning fails exactly the claimed 28 parametrized tests; parity/fastpath tests green, so the oracle sync note (single-file, equivalence-verified, parity green) is correctly specified. 11 matching call-site lines in test/bittypes_test.py confirmed (three lines contain two calls each, so call expressions number ~15 -- counting quibble only). All five moots genuine: string-6 adds the String class docstring; lows-docs-1 fixes float.py:225 prose and drops the pytypes type-annotations (62-73 half via accepted pytypes-1); lows-docs-2 fixes aggregate_types.py:185; docs-misc-1's repr moot is a disclosed design-decision won't-fix (accepted eval-able bits-form repr) rather than a fix -- honestly labeled 'do not re-litigate'. NITS: (1) 'plain suite: 855 passed' is off by one -- the suite is 854 (the 54-warning and 28-failure figures are exact, so the substance of the verification stands). (2) The live array()-docstring item overlaps lows-docs-3's accepted structs.py:655-657 edit (which already documents endian/default); the coordinate/merge note covers it, but it is closer to mooted than live.
